ACUTE_BRONCHITIS.title: Acute bronchitis (infection of the airways)

items: Acute bronchitis is an infection that inflames the large airways (breathing tubes) of the lungs.
The main sign is a cough. It usually lasts about 2 to 3 weeks, with an average of about 18 days.
A cough that may be dry or bring up mucus (sputum).
Coloured mucus does not, on its own, show that the infection is bacterial.
A chest X-ray is done only if pneumonia (infection of the lung tissue) is suspected.
Your doctor will decide on treatment after examining you.
Ask your doctor which medicines suit you and how to take them.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Expect the cough to last for a few weeks.
See your doctor if the cough is not settling after about 3 weeks, or if any warning sign below appears.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Breathing faster than 24 breaths a minute
Heart rate of 100 or more beats a minute
Temperature of 38 degrees C or more, with chest signs of pneumonia
